title: The 1961 Chemistry Nobel cited the carbon path in photosynthesis
summary: Melvin Calvin received the prize for work on carbon dioxide assimilation in plants.
body: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1961 was awarded to Melvin Calvin. The OpenStax page names the Calvin cycle as the sugar-building stage that uses ATP and NADPH from the light reactions. The prize page is the institutional citation; the textbook is the classroom map. Neither is a claim that the cycle is the only carbon-fixation pathway in all organisms.
